note: sections/02-geometry.tex: "Use exact dynamic programming also if $\ell<2^{1000}$ or $\ell\varepsilon<10$. It uses $O((N+1)^2)$ word operations", with H = least power of two >= ceil(log2(N+2)) and ell = least power of two >= log2 H. So the approximate branch needs N+2 > 2^(2^(2^999)) (and ell*eps >= 10 on top), and thm:main is pointwise in eps with eps-dependent thresholds.

Nine-Fourths paper.tex, sec:growth: "The definition of $\nu$ supplies a fixed integer $u\geq2$ and an exact rank decomposition of $T_u$ of length $r<u^{9/4+\delta}$" (never exhibited; nu<=9/4 itself rests on lem:existence, proved by separation, compactness and a fixed-point theorem), and sec:intro says the proof "does not specify a competitive finite matrix size". The companions say the same: Staggered thm:main omega_F<2.371054886006746 "do not give bit-complexity or practical crossover estimates", and 2.258 thm:main omega<1129/500 "does not claim a practical crossover size".

thm:main gives one multitape Turing machine with T_A(n)=O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}), kappa=2^{-182}, and eq:fixed-parameters sets epsilon=2^{-75}. In 08-assembly.tex b=ceil(log2 n) and d=floor(b^epsilon), so d>=2 iff b>=2^(2^75), i.e. n > 2^(2^(2^75)-1), with "schoolbook multiplication" below the cutoff.

thm:factorization gives O(((n+1)ceil(log2 p))^{10^{12}}); 08-driver calls p "small when $p\le B^{200000}$" (B=20+(n+1)(L+1)) and then tests gcd(h,b-a) for a=0..p-1, so the curve branch needs primes of at least about 4.6M bits. Unconditionality rests on Theorem analytic:hecke = [OpenAIPrimitive26, Thm 1.2] (family 029, strip Re s>1-10^{-6}, which the catalogue lists as not formalized).

thm:main: O(n(log n)^theta(log log n)^{4-theta}) with theta=log_m(m-Delta/W_*), m=10^6, W_*=2^71, Delta=6871402692000000, so 1-theta=2.106e-13 and cor:decimal gives O(n(log n)^{1-10^{-13}}); the paper says "The constants in the algorithm are enormous ... with no useful crossover estimate". Wording nit in prior.json: 2^71 is the number of batched arrays, not a block length, and the recursion only engages for transform length 2^k with k>=K=72*10^6.

zstd HEAD 49cf517: cover.c:483-490 and fastcover.c:140-147 score Score(S)=sum of F(dmer) and zero the covered dmers, and both build loops fill until tail==0 with segmentSize=MIN(...,tail), i.e. coverage under a byte budget with no superstring objective; ZDICT_trainFromBuffer (zdict.c:1111) defaults to fastCover. A rerun reproduced the segment logs byte for byte, and an independent cycle-cover bound equals greedy: 1,186 B = 1.053% (COVER) and 1,452 B = 1.289% (FASTCOVER) of 112,640, so the method is sound (the '1.06%' equals 1186/111454, i.e. divided by the merged length, not the dictionary size).

003 thm:main (Sept-30 paper.tex) covers only Hecke L-functions over Q(sqrt-3) "and every Dirichlet $L$-function" (the latter via eq:hecke-dirichlet-factorization, L_F(s,chi∘N)=L(s,chi)L(s,chi chi_{-3})); a class-group character of order >=3 of another quadratic field gives L(s,Ind psi), an irreducible 2-dimensional dihedral L-function, which is neither Dirichlet nor, apart from D4 edge cases, Hecke over Q(sqrt-3). Caveat: family 029 Thm 1.2 (all Hecke characters of cyclotomic F containing mu_12, width 10^{-6}, unformalized) does reach these by base change to Q(mu_lcm(12,|d|)), but only with galactic (log|d|)^{O(10^6)}-type bounds, so the 'keep GRH caveats' conclusion stands.
